title: Open a glass studio in Staunton: the master process and its decision points
question: I want to open a hot glass studio in Staunton (gas furnace, glory hole, kilns, torches, oxygen and propane, cold-working, public classes, maybe a small cafe or sip-and-blow events). Which city, state and health offices do I have to go through, in what order, and which choices change the path?
office: Community Development Department, Planning & Zoning Division (zoning and historic review) and Building Services Division (building, trade and occupancy permits); Staunton Fire & Rescue, Fire Marshal's Office (operational permits and inspections); Commissioner of the Revenue (business license and business property); Virginia Department of Health, Central Shenandoah Health District (food); Virginia ABC (alcohol); the Department of Economic Development is the office to ask about sites and incentives
summary: A hot glass studio is three businesses at once in the eyes of the City of Staunton: a small manufacturing shop (gas-fired furnace, glory hole, kilns and torches), a retail gallery and classroom open to the public, and, if you add a cafe or sip-and-blow events, a restaurant that may serve alcohol. The path is: (1) pick a site and confirm with Planning & Zoning that the use is allowed there, because the B-2 general business district allows processing only when it is incidental to retail on the premises and small, the I-1 light industrial district allows manufacturing from glass but limits retail, and any of the five downtown historic districts adds a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior work; (2) get the building, mechanical, gas and electrical permits and a certificate of occupancy for the new use from Building Services (apply in the online portal; commercial review is estimated at fifteen business days); (3) settle the Fire Marshal's operational permits for LP-gas, oxygen and other compressed gases, hot work and any assembly use before opening; (4) license the business with the Commissioner of the Revenue (minimum $30, retail at $0.20 per $100 of gross receipts above $50,000) and file the business tangible property return each May 1; (5) if you serve food or drink, add the Health District plan review and food establishment permit ($40 each), the 7% meals tax and a Virginia ABC license; (6) line up water and sewer, natural gas or propane, and check DEQ's air permit exemption for the furnace. Talk first to Planning & Zoning (540.332.3862); the Department of Economic Development (540.332.3869) is the office for sites, the Enterprise Zone and incentives. The sub-processes are modelled in the glass_studio_* files.

steps.step: Decide what the studio is: industrial shop, retail and teaching studio, or both
steps.how: Write down the equipment (gas furnace, glory hole, annealing and casting kilns, torches, oxygen and propane cylinders, cold-working wheels and saws, dust and fume exhaust), the public uses (gallery, classes, sip-and-blow events) and whether you will sell food or drink. The answers set the zoning district you can use, the building code occupancy group the building must meet, which Fire Marshal permits apply, and whether the health department and ABC are involved. In Staunton's zoning code a glass studio is not a named use: the business districts list retail, restaurants, schools and small retail-incidental processing, while the I-1 light industrial district lists manufacturing from previously prepared materials such as glass but allows retail only when it serves industrial plants. The Zoning Administrator decides which listed use your plan is closest to.
steps.deadline: Before you sign a lease or buy a building
steps.quote: Planning & Zoning is responsible for the review and processing of residential and commercial development applications within the City, including re-zonings, special use permits, comprehensive plan amendments, zoning approvals, zoning appeals, and zoning variances.

steps.step: Talk to Planning & Zoning first, then to the Department of Economic Development
steps.who: Studio owner; Community Development, Planning & Zoning Division (540.332.3862); Department of Economic Development (540.332.3869)
steps.how: Call or visit Planning & Zoning on the third floor of City Hall with the address or candidate addresses and the equipment and use list from step 1. Ask three things: whether the use is permitted by right, permitted on review (a special use permit through the Planning Commission and City Council) or not allowed in that district; whether the property is in one of the five historic districts or an entrance corridor; and whether a zoning permit and a certificate of occupancy for a change of use will be needed. For a written answer, request a Zoning Verification Letter (city estimate ten business days; $75 on the fee schedule as a Zoning Official Determination Letter). The Department of Economic Development, also on the third floor, is the office for available buildings and sites, the Enterprise Zone and other incentives (see glass_studio_zoning_use and the city's Economic Development site).
steps.fee: Zoning Official Determination Letter $75.00 (Planning & Zoning fee schedule); the conversation itself is free
steps.quote: Estimated Processing Time: Ten (10) business days.

steps.step: Pick the site with the zoning answer in hand (decision point: downtown historic district or not)
steps.how: Downtown Staunton lies largely in the Beverley and other historic districts, where the H-1 overlay requires a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Historic Preservation Commission for any material change to the exterior that is visible from a public street (new vents, flues, exhaust stacks, signs, doors, storefront changes), whether or not a building permit is needed; administrative staff review covers signs and screening of mechanical equipment, and other work goes to the Commission, which meets on the fourth Tuesday with a first-Tuesday agenda deadline. The Entrance Corridor Overlay District adds design guidelines on thirteen corridors. Outside those districts the exterior review falls away. If the only district that fits the furnace work is I-1, expect limits on the retail and class side; if the fit is B-2 with manufacturing incidental to retail, expect the city to look at the share of the floor and staff devoted to production. Where the use is listed as permitted on review, budget about three months and $250 for the special use permit.
steps.quote: The five historic districts are Gospel Hill, Beverley, The Wharf, Stuart Addition, and Newtown.

steps.step: Check whether a building is in the Staunton Enterprise Zone and ask Economic Development about incentives
steps.who: Studio owner; Department of Economic Development (office: City Hall, 3rd floor, 116 W. Beverley St., 540.332.3869)
steps.how: The city's Start a Business page says the Virginia Enterprise Zone covers most of the central business district and the West Beverley Street corridor and provides local and state tax and fee incentives to new or expanding business; the Economic Development site also names the West End Opportunity Zone and C-PACE clean-energy financing. The Plan Submittal Form for site plans asks whether the property is in the Enterprise Zone. Program rules and applications are not published on the pages read; the office asks businesses to contact it.
steps.quote: Staunton Economic Development provides powerful financial incentives specifically designed to aid new business establishment and accelerate existing business expansion.

steps.step: Get the zoning approvals (zoning permit, special use permit if needed, Certificate of Appropriateness if in a historic district)
steps.who: Studio owner; Planning & Zoning Division; Planning Commission and City Council (special use permit); Historic Preservation Commission
steps.how: Modelled in glass_studio_zoning_use. In short: a zoning permit ($50) or zoning approval for the use; a special use permit ($250, public hearings before the Planning Commission and City Council, about three months) where the use is permitted on review; a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior changes in a historic district (staff review about ten business days for signs and mechanical screening, otherwise the Commission's monthly meeting); and a sign permit (outside historic districts) or Certificate of Appropriateness for signage (inside them). Since May 5, 2026 these are applied for in the city's online permitting portal.
steps.deadline: Before the building permit; the city will not issue a building permit until zoning and, in a historic district, the Certificate of Appropriateness are in place
steps.fee: Zoning permit $50.00; special use permit $250.00; sign permit per fee schedule (see glass_studio_zoning_use)

steps.step: Get the building, mechanical, fuel-gas and electrical permits and the certificate of occupancy
steps.who: Studio owner, architect or engineer, licensed contractors; Community Development, Building Services Division (540.332.3862, permits@ci.staunton.va.us)
steps.how: Modelled in glass_studio_building_mechanical. A change of use to a shop with gas-fired furnaces, kilns and compressed gases is reviewed under the Virginia Construction Code; the building permit application asks for the use group and occupant load, and the trade permit application asks for the type of gas (natural gas, above-ground or in-ground LP), the number of fuel tanks and any commercial hoods. The city estimates fifteen business days for commercial review. Fees are set in City Code § 15.10.120 (for example commercial alteration $0.18 per square foot, $95 minimum; commercial trade permits $0.05 per square foot for alterations, $95 minimum; certificate of occupancy for an existing building $95). Real estate taxes on the property must be paid first.
steps.deadline: Before any construction, equipment installation or occupancy
steps.fee: Building and trade permit fees under City Code § 15.10.120 (amounts in glass_studio_building_mechanical)
steps.quote: Separate permits are required for electrical, plumbing, mechanical, and gas.

steps.step: Settle the Fire Marshal's operational permits and inspection before you fire up
steps.who: Studio owner; Staunton Fire & Rescue, Fire Marshal's Office (540.332.3720, firemarshals@ci.staunton.va.us)
steps.how: Modelled in glass_studio_fire_permits. The city's fire code fee schedule lists an LP-gas permit ($50 a year), a hazardous materials permit ($50 a year) and flammable and combustible liquids permits; the state Fire Prevention Code also lets the fire official require permits for compressed gases above set amounts (oxygen above 504 cubic feet, flammable gases above 200 cubic feet), hot work, industrial ovens, open flames in assembly or dining areas and places of assembly. Staunton's schedule does not price those, and the city's Fire Prevention Activity Application is for other activities not listed but require a permit, so ask the Fire Marshal which apply. Expect an inspection before the permit and at least yearly after.
steps.deadline: Before storing propane, oxygen or flammable gases on site and before opening to the public
steps.fee: LP-gas $50.00 a year; hazardous materials $50.00 a year; others as the Fire Marshal sets
steps.quote: The Fire Marshal’s Office issues the following permits, and permit fees are applied as specified in the city code.

steps.step: License the business with the Commissioner of the Revenue and register your equipment
steps.who: Studio owner; Commissioner of the Revenue (540-332-3829, revenue@ci.staunton.va.us)
steps.how: Modelled in glass_studio_business_license. One Staunton business license covers the studio's lines of business at one location if you elect it and accept the highest applicable rate; the license is $30 for gross receipts up to $50,000 and then $0.20 per $100 for retail or $0.36 per $100 for services such as classes. File within 30 days of opening (state law says before). Furnaces, kilns, tools and fixtures go on the business tangible personal property return by May 1 each year; machinery and tools used in manufacturing are a separate class taxed at $1.24 per $100. Also register any trade name with the State Corporation Commission and for Virginia sales tax.
steps.deadline: Business license within 30 days of starting business (city); business property return by May 1
steps.fee: Business license minimum $30.00; then by class and gross receipts
steps.quote: To avoid penalties and interest, you are required to file an application within 30 days of when you begin to conduct business.

steps.step: Decision point: cafe or not, alcohol or not, public events or not
steps.who: Studio owner; Virginia Department of Health, Central Shenandoah Health District (540-332-7830); Virginia ABC; Commissioner of the Revenue; Parks & Recreation (special events)
steps.how: Modelled in glass_studio_food_and_events. Selling prepared food or drinks makes the studio a restaurant under state law: health department plan review ($40) and a food establishment permit ($40, apply at least 30 days before opening), the 7% city meals tax with monthly returns, and a Virginia ABC retail license (wine and beer on- and off-premises $450 state fee a year, local tax up to $150, 60 to 90 days of processing) if you pour. An ABC retail license cannot be used to sell or serve until the health permit issues. One-off sip-and-blow nights without a restaurant can run on ABC banquet licenses ($40 a day); pouring free wine at an art walk needs an annual arts venue event license ($300, up to 12 days a year). Food at an outdoor event needs a temporary food establishment permit ($40, ten calendar days ahead), and an event on city streets or parks needs the city's special event application 60 days ahead.
steps.quote: Once a Plan Review is approved, submit a completed Foodservice Permit Application, along with a $40.00 application fee, at least 30 days prior to opening for approval.

steps.step: Line up utilities and environmental approvals
steps.who: Studio owner; Public Works (water and sewer, 540.332.3892); Engineering Division (new connections, 540.332.3858); Columbia Gas of Virginia or a propane supplier; Environmental Programs Division (land disturbance); DEQ Valley Regional Office (air)
steps.how: Modelled in glass_studio_utilities_and_environment. A new or larger water meter needs the Water and Sewer Connection and Facility Fee application before the building permit (fees are set by meter size: for a 3/4-inch meter the 2025-26 schedule shows $5,250 water and $10,280 sewer facilities fees plus connection fees); cold-working water goes to the city sewer, whose pretreatment chapter (City Code ch. 13.55) may require a wastewater survey. Natural gas is from Columbia Gas of Virginia (new business line 1-800-440-6111; a gas availability form gets a call back within two business days); propane is a Fire Marshal matter. Site work over 10,000 square feet needs a land disturbing permit ($3,000 plus a $2,500-per-acre bond). A gas-fired glass furnace and glory hole are fuel-burning equipment; DEQ's minor new source review exempts gaseous-fuel units under 50,000,000 Btu per hour, but the owner must keep records showing the exemption applies and should check with the Valley Regional Office in Harrisonburg.
steps.deadline: Water and sewer application before the building permit; gas service before the mechanical final
steps.quote: The City of Staunton provides water, sewer, trash and recycling services. All other utilities are provided by private companies (listed below).

steps.step: Open: final inspections, certificate of occupancy, fire inspection, health inspection
steps.who: Building Services inspectors; Fire Marshal's Office; Health District environmental health specialist; studio owner
steps.how: Request the building, mechanical, gas and electrical finals in the online portal; the building official issues the certificate of occupancy within five working days after the final inspection is approved (a temporary commercial certificate costs $250 for 60 days). The Fire Marshal inspects before issuing operational permits and at least yearly afterwards. A food establishment gets a pre-opening inspection and is inspected at least annually. Post the permits and the certificate on the premises.
steps.fee: Commercial temporary certificate of occupancy $250.00 for 60 days (City Code § 15.10.120, read on eCode360)
steps.quote: The building official shall issue the certificate of occupancy within five working days after approval of the final inspection and when the building or structure or portion thereof is determined to be in compliance with this code and any pertinent laws or ordinances, or when otherwise entitled.

escalation.trigger: The Zoning Administrator determines that the studio is not a permitted use, or attaches conditions you dispute
escalation.next: Board of Zoning Appeals (appeal of the Zoning Administrator's decision; $200 on the Planning & Zoning fee schedule), then the Staunton Circuit Court
escalation.quote: The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.

escalation.next: Appeal to City Council, then to the Staunton Circuit Court (City Code § 18.85.050(n), read on eCode360: 30 days to Council, 30 days from Council's decision to court)
escalation.deadline: Petition to the circuit court within 30 days after the governing body's final decision
escalation.quote: provided that the petition is filed within 30 days after the final decision is rendered by the governing body

escalation.trigger: Disagreement with the building official's application of the building code
escalation.next: Local Board of Building Code Appeals, then the State Building Code Technical Review Board
escalation.deadline: Written appeal within 30 calendar days of receiving the decision
escalation.quote: The applicant shall submit a written request for appeal to the LBBCA within 30 calendar days of the receipt of the decision being appealed.

escalation.next: Local board of appeals, then the State Building Code Technical Review Board

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) answers HTTP 403 to automated readers, so every city page and PDF cited here is an Internet Archive copy (capture dates are given in sources). The Historic Preservation Districts page could only be read in a 2021 capture and the Economic Development department page in a 2017 capture; the live pages may differ.

Local law not quoted. The Staunton City Code is published on eCode360, whose terms forbid reproducing its text for public purposes. Section numbers and links are given, and the zoning rules are paraphrased from a reading of chapters 18.15, 18.55, 18.60, 18.75, 18.85, 18.195, 18.205, 18.210 and 18.220 and of §§ 15.10.120 and 15.25.055 on 2026-10-19. Fee amounts from those sections are reported as figures, not quoted.

No zoning district names a glass studio, artisan manufacturing or a craft school. Which listed use a hot shop with classes is closest to, and whether it is permitted by right, on review, or not at all in a given building, is the Zoning Administrator's determination. Only a conversation or a Zoning Verification Letter settles it.

The building code occupancy classification of a hot shop with a gallery and classroom (factory, mercantile, business, educational or assembly, or a mix) and whether a sprinkler, exhaust or separation is required are design questions decided in plan review by the Building Official; they are not researched here.

The Fire Marshal's local fee schedule (§ 15.25.055) lists LP-gas, hazardous materials, flammable and combustible liquids, explosives, pyrotechnics, tents and a few other permits, but no entries for compressed gases, hot work, industrial ovens, open flames or places of assembly, which the state code lists as permits the fire official may require. Whether Staunton requires them, and at what fee, was not confirmed.
Staff names and personal mailboxes printed on city pages and forms are omitted; only office lines, office addresses and role mailboxes are recorded.

The Economic Development office's incentive rules and applications are not on the pages read; the Start a Business page's description of the Enterprise Zone is from a 2026 capture of a page whose program details may have changed.

Not confirmed by lexflow's software: the words once quoted for the step 'Get the zoning approvals (zoning permit, special use permit if needed, Certificate of Appr' (https://www.ci.staunton.va.us/departments/community-development/apply-online) were not found on the cited page as lexflow read it (not found word for word in the Internet Archive copy of 10 June 2026 of the cited page, read on 11 October 2026). Those claims now rest on the cited page as read, without a matched quote; check them at the link before relying on them.
